title: Personal AI agent apps: how to pick one that fits your day
h1: a personal ai agent that fits your actual day
description: What a personal AI agent app does, four kinds worth comparing, where each one runs and the full bill, plus a small first job to try before you commit.
keywords: best ai agents for personal use
what is a personal ai agent
answer: **a personal ai agent is an assistant that keeps an ongoing job for you, with memory, app access and repeat work.** stop reintroducing the same project every time you need a hand. choose where you talk, what it may reach and whether it must work with your laptop off. dusk gives each bot its own chats and memory. a texting service, cloud task agent or workflow builder may fit better.

review.by: lead agent: read against seo/facts, automated gate, independent fact-check pass

og_line: choose around a job, not a promise.

table.intro: **choose the kind of help you will come back to tomorrow.** competitor details are as of 12 november 2026. start with where you talk and who keeps the work running.

sections.h: start with this week’s annoying job
sections.md:
**give it the annoying job you already understand.** choose material you can hand over and an answer you can judge:

- compare two documents
- prepare questions before an appointment
- review notes for a small project

then ask what would make the next attempt easier: memory, app access, repetition or work while you are away. a single question may need no ongoing agent.

try the same task across products. compare what each missed and how much context you had to repeat. your real mess tells you more than a polished demo.

sections.h: what makes it an agent, not a chatbot
sections.md:
**an agent keeps the job between conversations.** a chatbot answers the question in front of it. a personal agent carries on:

- **memory:** it keeps what you tell it and facts it notices in your messages.[^7]
- **app access:** it reads and drafts in apps you connect, and asks before sending unless you set a daily amount.[^8]
- **repeat work:** it runs a routine on a schedule or when an app event arrives.[^13]
- **a computer of its own:** some get a browser and desktop separate from yours.[^14]

you may not need all four. a weekly summary needs repeat work and app access, not a computer.

sections.h: choose a conversation you will return to
sections.md:
**pick somewhere you will remember to text it.** [poke](/alternatives/poke) supports apple messages, telegram, whatsapp and rcs. it fits if your existing chat app is where you want the helper.[^3]

dusk has desktop chats and its own phone app. on iphone, get it from the app store; on android, download the .apk from dusk.bot/download until it reaches google play. the app tells you when a reply, question or approval arrives.[^6]

pairing to your computer needs it awake with dusk running. pairing to dusk cloud works with your computer off. try [phone access](/claude-code-from-your-phone) under the conditions you expect to use.

sections.h: tell it once, then keep the memory useful
sections.md:
**teach it the preference you keep repeating.** each dusk bot keeps its own memory. about me in settings shares your name, time zone and writing preferences with all bots.

read and edit notes in memory settings when an assumption changes. turning off let this bot use memory leaves the files on disk.[^7]

start connected apps read only. if you grant writes later, say "ask me before you change anything"; app edits do not automatically ask.[^8]

your text goes from the bot’s machine to your chosen ai provider. local storage and local ai are separate choices. ollama and lm studio offer the local-model route.[^1]

**add up the work, the computer and any license you need.** as of 12 november 2026, dusk’s desktop app includes every feature free for personal use. work needs a license. your ai provider bills usage separately.

cloud prices cover the computer, with ai separate:[^9]

- plus: $20 monthly or $200 yearly
- pro: $50 monthly or $500 yearly

poke lists free and pro at $19 monthly. manus lists free and pro at $20 monthly with 4,000 monthly credits.[^10][^11] look at what your job consumes before comparing prices.

when a dusk bot’s ai plan runs out, it tells you. wait for the reset or switch ai. cloud hosting keeps the machine awake; it does not add ai allowance.

**pick dusk when you want a helper whose work stays together.** give bots distinct jobs and memory. change a bot’s model without losing its chats, files or notes.

mainly need research or a presentation? try [manus](/alternatives/manus) on that task. enjoy mapping and maintaining a visual process? look at [n8n](/alternatives/n8n). want the helper inside whatsapp or imessage? poke lives there; dusk bots live in dusk's own apps.[^3][^6]

its code is source-available under polyform noncommercial, not open source. personal and work use have different terms.[^12]

**give a new agent less power than you think it needs.** keep a new dusk bot on **ask for approval** for a few days, then loosen up.[^15] emails, messages and posts wait for your allow unless you set a daily amount.[^8]

careful with **Full access**: a bot there with no sending rule can send up to 25 a day without asking. give it **Ask every time**.

don't hand it your bank yet. let it earn trust on a job where a mistake costs you a minute, not money.

sections.h: try one helper before making a team
sections.md:
**make the first conversation worth continuing.** attach a non-sensitive document you know and ask: "prepare questions about this document. separate what it says from questions i should ask. contact nobody and change no files."

read the questions beside the source. give a correction and try a related task. does keeping the conversation save you from explaining it all again?

add a routine when the job has a clear repeat. if setup and review cost more effort than the task, narrow it. keep the helper because you use it.

faq.q: what is a personal ai agent?
faq.a: **an assistant that keeps working on your jobs, not just answering one question.** it remembers what you tell it, works in apps you connect and can repeat a task on a schedule. some also get a browser and desktop of their own. you talk to it in an app or a chat channel.[^7][^8][^13][^14]

faq.q: can a personal ai agent be free?
faq.a: **dusk’s desktop app is free for personal use, with every feature.** your ai provider bills usage, and cloud hosting is separate. as of 12 november 2026, poke lists a free tier and pro at $19 a month; manus lists free and pro at $20 a month. compare allowances with your actual job.[^9][^10][^11]

faq.q: what is the best personal ai agent app?
faq.a: **the one that fits where you already talk and what you need done.** poke suits texting in apple messages, telegram or whatsapp. manus suits finished cloud tasks. n8n suits people who build workflows. dusk suits separate named bots with their own memory, on your computer, a cloud or your server.[^1][^3][^4][^5]

faq.q: how do i use dusk from a phone?
faq.a: **get the app and pair it to the machine holding your bots.** iphone uses the app store; android uses the .apk from dusk.bot/download, as it is not on google play yet. paired with your computer, that computer must be on. paired with dusk cloud, it works with your computer off.[^6]

faq.q: must a personal agent run in the cloud?
faq.a: **no, choose where the work needs to happen.** dusk bots can live on your computer, cloud or server. local routines stop when the computer sleeps or dusk closes.
